solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lengthens leases foremost of dukes hold

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it out

indicators.note: the foremost letter of the word dukes is the one taken

parts.note: to hold something is to own it

explanation.surface: A legal note about tenancies being extended while the dukes keep their estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressmaker lengthens a skirt or trousers by letting out the hem, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Large cola ordered in neighbourhood pub

parts.note: L is the standard clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, as if arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a big cola at the pub round the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a drinker's request, but it signals rearranging L and COLA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the pub nearest home, the one regularly visited, is called your local.

clue.text: Worker, having drink after time, displays a fit of temper

indicators.note: the worker-plus-drink piece is placed after the time letter

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: An employee who has been drinking at work loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a childish outburst of rage, so it is a synonym for a fit of temper.

clue.text: Girl on sailing boat makes a delivery

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Daisy is a girl's name
a cutter is a single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A girl aboard a yacht is bringing a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests the post, but it is a cricket term: a bowled ball that skims along the ground is a daisy-cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket each ball bowled is a delivery, and a daisy-cutter is one that barely rises off the grass.

clue.text: Pull young girl across river

indicators.note: the girl's word stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: wench is an old word for a young woman
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone drags a young girl to the far bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench is to twist or tug violently, so it is a synonym for pull.

clue.text: Ring up about second musical work

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone phones back within a second about a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin for 'work', used to number a composer's compositions.

clue.text: Earlier religious building, incomplete

indicators.note: the building's word is left without its final letter

parts.note: a priory is a house of monks or nuns

explanation.surface: An old place of worship that was never finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means coming before in time, a synonym for earlier.

clue.text: Frank's following on

definitions.note: read as 'Frank is', the 's being a link; frank means candid, an adjective

parts.note: since means after, as in 'since the war'
re means on or about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A man called Frank is next in line to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank person speaks honestly and openly, which is what a sincere person does.

clue.text: Tory side helping, thinking of others

parts.note: CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a ration is a portion or helping of food

explanation.surface: A Conservative's portion of food, a contrast with being selfless.
explanation.definitionFit: Consideration is thoughtful regard for the feelings and needs of other people.

clue.text: Hear Stuarts rebuilt this Scottish landmark

indicators.note: the letters are taken apart and put together again in a new structure

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen as the royal Stuarts reconstruct a Scottish monument.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTHUR'S SEAT is the extinct volcano overlooking Edinburgh; the Stuarts were Scotland's royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's Seat is the hill in Holyrood Park, Edinburgh, a famous Scottish landmark.

clue.text: Vehicle coming from Ayr rolled over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the run of letters is read backwards
the letters are taken from within the words Ayr rolled

explanation.surface: A vehicle from the Scottish town of Ayr tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' looks like the reversal signal, but it belongs to the hidden letters; 'over' alone turns YRROL round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry is the British word for a truck, a heavy goods vehicle.

clue.text: Exclusive group from lake bed shown first

indicators.note: the bed word is placed before the lake word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A select set of people coming from a lakeside bed display.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small, select circle of people sharing interests and excluding outsiders.

clue.text: Chinese food: turn down whole lot

parts.note: to dim a light is to turn it down
the sum is the total, the whole lot

explanation.surface: Someone rejects an entire takeaway order of Chinese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn down' suggests refusing the food, but it means lowering a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Cantonese dumplings and snacks, a type of Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Lose heart, as pride injured

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone becomes discouraged because their pride has been hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up hope, which is what losing heart means.

clue.text: Chase funds university invested

indicators.note: invested means clothed or enclosed, so the university letter is put inside

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money, funds available

explanation.surface: A university puts money into a hunt for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' looks financial, but here it means placed within.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue is to follow in order to catch, a synonym for chase.

clue.text: Defiant remark made by heavy drinker in this place

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A drunk makes a cheeky retort in this very spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a childish retort of defiance, said after making a point.

clue.text: Cheery one, a learner driver after information

indicators.note: the information word comes first, the other pieces following it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the plate shown on a learner driver's car in Britain

explanation.surface: A cheerful learner driver following the route information.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers must display L-plates, so L stands for learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means friendly and good-humoured, a synonym for cheery.

clue.text: Surprise the Parisian after dawn

indicators.note: the French article follows the word for beginning

parts.note: the dawn of something is its start
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Catching a Frenchman unawares at daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give a sudden shock or fright, a synonym for surprise.

clue.text: Iron block, a feature of Elizabethan village

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's tool was part of every sixteenth-century English village.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block a blacksmith hammers metal on.

clue.text: Found group in a cheerful mood

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
to be up is to be in high spirits

explanation.surface: Someone discovered a band of people feeling happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company or society is to establish it, as a phrasal verb says.

clue.text: Small-minded, rather lacking in character, ultimately

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: pretty means rather, as in 'pretty good'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word character

explanation.surface: Someone narrow-minded who, in the end, has rather little personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty means concerned with trivial things, mean-spirited, a synonym for small-minded.

clue.text: Notice plug

definitions.meaning: a public notice announcing goods or services
a plug is a piece of publicity for a product

explanation.definitionFit: Both a printed notice and a promotional plug are ways of publicising something for sale.

clue.text: Function of register announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a register

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a register's job is, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the part or job something plays, a synonym for its function.

clue.text: Flannel and soft soap

definitions.meaning: flannel is British slang for smooth, insincere talk
soft soap is persuasive praise used to win someone over

explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for excessive, insincere praise meant to please someone.
